title: Frictionless API Bootstraps: Quickstart Frames & Pricing Language
content:
TL;DR:
This brief proposes a compact set of developer-first value props, three distinct quickstart flows with suggested microcopy, and three pricing-language experiments aimed at reducing friction and clarifying unit economics for early adopters of the Hosted API. Goal is a short copy playbook we can A/B test on landing pages, signup flows and SDK readmes over the next quarter.

Audience:
- Primary: Individual engineers and small product teams evaluating an LLM API to ship an MVP in 1–2 weeks.
- Secondary: Platform/infra leads evaluating hosted choices for predictable latency and integration ease.

Overarching positioning (developer-first RTT):
- Build fast: trivial auth, ready-made SDK snippets, one-file demo apps.
- Predictable cost: clear per-inference units, dev-friendly cost calculators, free trial credits tied to realistic workloads.
- Production-ready: explicit latency/throughput profiles, Observable defaults (SLOs, traces) in the console.

Core value props (short lines for hero/CTA):
- "From zero to inference — one file, five lines, real responses."
- "Transparent pricing, predictable latency, production controls."
- "Ship LLM features without running GPUs — plug in and scale."

Quickstart flows (3 canonical developer journeys):
1) "Hello, endpoint" (5-minute flow) — For quick evaluation and demoing.
   - Steps: Sign up -> copy API key -> curl example -> see streaming response.
   - Microcopy highlights: "Copy API key (read-only dev scope)", "Try now — output in your terminal", "Streaming enabled by default for interactive demos".
   - KPI to measure: time-to-first-token, signups->curl-run conversion.

2) "SDK integrate" (15–30 minutes) — For productizing a single feature (chat, summarize).
   - Steps: Install SDK -> import client -> 5-line example -> add to 1 route in dev app.
   - Microcopy highlights: "Install: npm i @redwood/infer", "Auto-retry for transient errors (opt-in)", "Local dev key is safe for prototype, revoke later".
   - KPI: install->call success rate, sample app fork/clone rate.

3) "Launch-to-staging" (1–2 days) — Team onboarding with observability and cost controls.
   - Steps: Create org -> invite teammates -> pin model & rollout policy -> enable cost cap alert -> deploy to staging.
   - Microcopy highlights: "Pin a model version for repeatability", "Canary rollout: 10% traffic to new model", "Set a soft spend cap to avoid surprises".
   - KPI: time to configure staging route, alerts triggered in first week.

Pricing-language experiments (3 variants to test simultaneously):
A) Token-centric clarity (baseline): plain per-1k tokens & per-embedding rates, plus a developer trial with 50k tokens.
   - Pros: familiar to NLP teams.
   - Cons: confusing to product-first developers.

B) Action-based units (experiment): price by "API call type" (e.g., small-call, chat-turn, embed) with sample examples mapping to token ranges.
   - Example copy: "Small call (single prompt + short reply): $0.0008", "Chat-turn (multi-utterance): $0.003 per turn".
   - Pros: reduces mental math for non-ML engineers.
   - Cons: needs strong docs mapping to tokens for advanced users.

C) Outcome bundles (experiment): pre-bundled packages for common features (e.g., 1k summaries, 500k embed ops) + per-second compute tier for realtime streams.
   - Example copy: "Starter: 1k summaries + 10k embeddings — $19", "Realtime: billed by compute-second for streaming endpoints".
   - Pros: easy price anchoring for product teams, predictable budget lines.

Recommended starting experiment: run B + token-visible toggle. Default to action-based labels on marketing pages; expose raw token meters in console/SDK for power users.

Competitive note (how to contrast with two typical rivals):
- Generic cloud AI endpoints: emphasize lower integration friction and pre-built dev defaults (SDK snippets, streaming, ready rollouts).
- Model-only vendors: emphasize unified runtime + observability + cost controls; call out our predictable dedicated path for scale.

Sample microcopy bank (for page, SDK README, signup emails):
- Landing hero: "Integrate in minutes. Scale with confidence."
- Signup success: "Welcome! Your dev key is active for 30 days and includes a 50k token trial."
- CLI readme snippet: "redwood infer --sample 'Summarize this' — first 10 calls free"
- Console alert: "Estimated spend this week: $12 (projected $48) — set a cap"

Measurement plan (A/B + telemetry):
- Primary lift metrics: time-to-first-call, trial->paid conversion, average revenue per developer in month 1.
- Secondary: docs install completion, sample app forks, support ticket volume for billing questions.
- Variants to run: Pricing names (Token vs Action vs Bundle), Quickstart landing CTAs, Microcopy for cost controls.

Open questions / risks:
- Do we want to hide token math behind an "advanced" toggle in the public docs? (UX vs transparency tradeoff)
- Legal/compliance review for any "free trial" language tied to credits and auto-billing.
- Backend: can we export per-route "estimated cost per call" from runtime to UI in time for launch metrics?

Next steps (owner: Maya):
- Draft landing page copy for Action-based pricing + token toggle (due 2026-03-05).
- Coordinate with product to expose estimated cost per call in console API (engineering ticket GTM-ops backlog).
- Prepare A/B experiment in Growth: two landing pages + pricing modal variants (run for 6 weeks).

Notes to reviewers: This brief is intentionally pragmatic and focused on measurable experiments. Prefer concise action-based naming for marketing but keep transparency for developer console and SDKs. Feedback requested on: ideal free-trial size, microcopy tone (playful vs neutral), and whether we should include compute-second billing for streaming now or later.
